name: Amniota
blurb: Mammals and reptiles, birds included: animals whose embryos develop inside protective membranes, freeing them from laying eggs in water.

fossilMin.formation: Joggins Formation (division 4, section XV, coal group 15), Nova Scotia, Canada
fossilMin.dating: Palynomorph biostratigraphy: Langsettian (late Bashkirian), 319–318 Ma on GTS2012
fossilMin.checked: Benton et al. 2015, full text (palaeo-electronica.org/content/pdfs/424.pdf), node 47 (Crown Amniota)

softMax.basis: No diapsid or synapsid in the older, richly fossiliferous Little Cliff Shale, East Kirkton (Brigantian, late Viséan; 330.9 Ma plus up to 2 Myr)
softMax.checked: Benton et al. 2015, full text (palaeo-electronica.org/content/pdfs/424.pdf), node 47 (Crown Amniota)

challenge.taxon: Clawed crown-amniote trackways (NMV P258240), most probably made by a primitive sauropsid
challenge.formation: Home Station Sandstone Member, Snowy Plains Formation, Mansfield Basin, Victoria, Australia
challenge.checked: Long et al. 2025, main text (Europe PMC PMC12119326)
challenge.note: If these tracks are accepted as crown amniotes, the minimum rises to about 354 Ma, older than the 332.9 Ma soft maximum above, and this calibration needs revising. Footprints are less secure than skeletons: Benton et al. 2015 make the same point about older Nova Scotia tracks. This study treats Hylonomus itself as a crown amniote.

clock.method: Bayesian relaxed molecular clock (PhyloBayes, CAT-GTR), calibration scheme C16; mean and conservative 95% credibility interval (extremes of the 95% CIs of 100 gene-jackknife timetrees)
clock.checked: Irisarri et al. 2017, Supplementary Table 9, node 106 ("Amniotes")
